cf.title: Fix WITHOUT OVERLAPS PKs used for functional grouping

input.subject: Fix WITHOUT OVERLAPS PKs used for functional grouping

verdict_reasoning: The patch fixes a wrong-results bug that a committer reported, and the reporter backed the narrow fix in message #4. One fixable design point survived, replication-ondisk-1: views stored on 18.x that rely on a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key are not re-checked and fail later at restore or pg_upgrade. That is a backpatch decision for a committer who knows the area, and it does not question the fix itself.

brief.title: Stop using WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary keys for functional grouping
brief.problem: The planner accepts a WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key as proof of functional dependency for GROUP BY, but grouping uses the default btree equality and the key uses GiST equality. When they differ, as with citext, queries that select ungrouped columns are accepted and can return wrong results. Andres Freund reported it; it affects users of temporal primary keys.
brief.proposed_design: check_functional_grouping accepts only btree indexes, so a WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key no longer proves functional dependency. The author defers a finer check that compares each key column's equality operator with the grouping equality, to a later release unless reviewers accept it for backpatch.
user_visible_surface: Queries that group by a WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key and select other columns now fail with an error instead of returning rows.
author_claims: The fix is simple enough to backpatch through 18.
citext is the only built-in case found that shows the bug, because btree_gist has no citext opclass and GiST uses gist_text_ops by binary coercion.
Matching GiST and btree equality procs could later allow functional grouping again.
brief.thread_state: Yilin Zhang showed that a previously working query now errors; Andres Freund replied that this is the intended effect and backed the simpler fix. The rest of the thread is about whether bug reports belong in separate threads; Peter Eisentraut is the listed reviewer but has not posted.
unclear: The material does not say how many existing applications rely on functional grouping with temporal primary keys, so the backpatch break is unsized.
The patch does not say whether release notes will warn about queries that start to fail after a minor upgrade.
Nobody answered whether citext columns getting case-sensitive GiST comparisons needs a separate fix outside WITHOUT OVERLAPS.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Add GROUP BY ALL".
prior_attempts.quote: This caused the query to return wrong results when ORDER BY specifies non-default equality semantics.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit ef38a4d9756db9ae1d20f40aa39f3cf76059b81a which
implemented the GROUP BY ALL syntax, as well as 2ce745836 which
made some comment improvements therein.

A postcommit review discovered that GROUP BY ALL missed our special
handling of entries that also appear in an ORDER BY in the query.
This caused the query to return wrong results when ORDER BY
specifies non-default equality semantics.  While this should be
fixable with some refactoring, doing it cleanly seems like too
much code churn for late beta.  We'll revert and try again in v20.

The reverted commit also included some additional comment wordsmithing
and docs cleanup, which are retained as they weren't connected to the
reverted feature.

catversion bump needed due to change in struct Query.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P11 reverted a new grouping feature that ignored non-default equality semantics. This patch removes an existing inference with the same class of flaw and also takes the narrow route.

objections.title: Stored views that use the temporal key break later dump and upgrade
objections.failure_scenario: On 18.0, a user creates a view that groups by a WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key and selects other columns. After the minor update, the stored view still runs and can still return wrong results for citext. The failure appears later, when pg_dump restore or pg_upgrade to 19 recreates the view and hits the new error partway through.
objections.argument: Functional grouping is checked only at parse analysis, and the view records a pg_depend entry on the primary key constraint, so existing views are not re-validated. The commit message and message #1 cover new queries only, and the brief notes nothing about release notes. With Backpatch-through: 18, this catalog state is already in released clusters. Message #4 backs the simpler fix, but no message covers objects that already exist.
objections.author_must_show: How will users on 18.x find views and rules that already depend on a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key for functional grouping, before a dump or pg_upgrade fails on them?

critic.reasoning: Postgres checks functional grouping only at parse analysis, so a view stored on 18.x keeps working until a restore or pg_upgrade re-parses it and fails. The thread and commit message do not cover stored views or release notes.

refuted.title: Existing views on temporal keys may fail dump and restore after minor upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: On 18.x a user creates a view that groups by a WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key and selects other columns. After a minor upgrade the view still sits in the catalog. A later pg_dump or pg_upgrade into a patched server fails when the view definition is replayed, often during a migration or a restore from backup.
refuted.argument: Postgres records a dependency on the primary key constraint when a view relies on functional grouping, so such views exist on 18.x today. The fix makes the same definition fail with an error, but nothing in the commit message or the thread covers objects that are already stored. The thread discussed queries that start to fail (messages #2 and #4) but not stored definitions that dump cannot restore. A committer would likely ask for a release-note warning and a way to find affected views before backpatching to 18.
refuted.author_must_show: How will users on 18.x find views that depend on a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key for grouping, and what do release notes tell them to do before upgrading?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which describes the same stored-view failure more precisely.

refuted.title: Backpatch breaks correct range-type queries to fix a citext case
refuted.failure_scenario: An application that uses temporal keys on range columns, as in message #2, runs a grouping query whose results are correct. After a minor upgrade the query fails with an error. The users find out in production, and they never had the citext problem.
refuted.argument: Message #1 names citext through gist_text_ops as the only built-in case that gives wrong results. Range and btree_gist scalar types use the same equality proc in GiST and btree, so their results were correct. Andres preferred the simpler fix (message #4), and the author offered the per-column equality check as a backpatch option. A minor release that turns working queries into errors usually needs a stronger case than one extension type.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is the per-column equality-proc check riskier to backpatch than an error for every existing temporal-key grouping query on 18?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 raised this exact case. In message #4 Andres Freund weighed it and backed the simpler fix because the feature is new, and the commit message calls the per-column check too ambitious for a backpatch.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade re-creates stored views that group by a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key, and the new error can stop it.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch changes check_functional_grouping in pg_constraint.c; existing pg_depend entries from views on the temporal key stay.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The set of queries accepted under functional dependency for GROUP BY becomes smaller.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: A WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key no longer proves functional dependency, so some queries now fail at parse analysis.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A dump of a view created on 18.x that relies on the temporal key fails to restore on a patched server.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message says Backpatch-through: 18, and working queries start to fail after a minor update.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How will users on 18.x find views and rules that already depend on a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key for functional grouping, before a dump or pg_upgrade fails on them?
Will the release notes warn that queries grouping by a WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary key can start to fail after the minor update, and say how to rewrite them?
Should existing views that rely on a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key keep running after the minor update, given that they can still return wrong results for citext?
Does a citext column that gets case-sensitive GiST comparisons through gist_text_ops need a separate fix outside WITHOUT OVERLAPS?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund reported the bug and backed the simpler fix in the thread; Peter Eisentraut is the listed reviewer but has not posted. The owner needs to know parse analysis of GROUP BY and the temporal key code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in a minor release of 18: working queries start to fail, and stored views can fail at a later restore or pg_upgrade. The code change itself is small and adds nothing to maintain.
committability.author_follow_up: The author offers in message #1 to update the patch with the per-column equality check and to send follow-up patches for v20.

priority.reason: This is a wrong-results fix for users of temporal primary keys, in one backend file plus regression tests. The open point is how the backpatch treats views already stored on 18.x, which a release note and a catalog query can cover.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that the check accepts only btree indexes and leaves ordinary primary keys alone is unverified. Whether stored views are in fact not re-checked after the update rests on the surviving objection's description.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: deferred primary key and logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed logical replication so that a table whose primary key is deferrable can be used as the replica identity, allowing UPDATE and DELETE on such tables to be replicated. It included a test covering this case.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila noted that the documentation requires replica identity indexes to be non-deferrable, and that a deferrable primary key should not be treated differently from a deferrable unique constraint. The author then said the patch was probably wrong because RelationGetIndexList() is also used by other backend modules. Amit Kapila added that logical decoding of in-progress transactions is supported starting in PG-14, which undercuts the argument that only finished transactions are decoded. The author did not respond after that, and the entry was returned with feedback because there was no response and it was unclear whether the change is possible.

precedents_retrieved.summary: A bug report: after dump and restore, a column covered only by a DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY loses attnotnull, because pg_dump emits a throwaway NOT NULL constraint and then drops it. The author's patch changes pg_dump to skip the throwaway NOT NULL constraint for deferrable primary keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. precedents_retrieved.title: Add sortsupport for range types and btree_gist
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add sortsupport functions to the range type GiST opclass and to all btree_gist opclasses, so GiST indexes on these types use the sorted build method by default. The goal is faster index builds and better index structure, for example for exclusion constraints.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In March 2024 Andrey Borodin asked that tests from his earlier, similar patch be ported, possibly with injection points. Bernd Helmle moved the entry back to Waiting on Author, and the visible messages show no updated patch before it was returned in October 2024. Earlier, Bernd Helmle had measured a pgbench regression for a sorted-built int4 btree_gist index, from about 213k to 125k tps, but the visible messages do not show that as the deciding reason.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: FWIW it would be nice at least port tests from commit that I referenced upthread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove useless GROUP BY columns considering unique index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets remove_useless_groupby_columns use unique constraints whose columns are all NOT NULL, in addition to the primary key, to drop functionally dependent GROUP BY columns. When several candidates exist, it picks the one with the fewest columns so that the most columns can be removed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch no longer applied because it relied on catalogued NOT NULL constraints, which had been removed. David Rowley also objected to choosing the constraint with the fewest columns, which ignores column width and can pick a constraint with no columns in the GROUP BY clause, a regression against today's primary-key behaviour. The author said he would study the advice and update, but the visible messages show no new version before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It looks like it  won't work if the UNIQUE constraint with
the least columns gets no mention in the GROUP BY clause. That'll
cause performance regressions from what we have today when the primary
key is mentioned and columns can be removed using that but a UNIQUE
constraint exists which has no corresponding GROUP BY columns and
fewer unique columns than the PK.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: enum support in btree_gin and btree_gist
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds enum support to the btree_gin and btree_gist extensions, without distance operators and so without KNN support. The enum comparison goes through enum_cmp_internal, which uses the type cache for enums whose values are not in OID order.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Testing showed that GiST comparisons gave wrong results after alter type ... add value, because enum_cmp_internal expects fcinfo->flinfo and DirectFunctionCallN passes NULL. Tom Lane judged a NULL check too slow and said the proper fix is to pass the FunctionCallInfo through the btree_gist/gin intermediate layer, which touches almost every function. The author agreed but had no time to do this before the end of the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem is that the intermediate layer in btree_gist (and
probably btree_gin too, didn't look) does not pass through the
FunctionCallInfo data structure that's provided by the GIST AM.

precedents_retrieved.title: Temporal foreign key actions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds RESTRICT, CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT actions for temporal foreign keys, plus preparatory patches that add FOR PORTION OF details to TriggerData and make ExecForPortionOfLeftovers obey EXEC_FLAG_SKIP_TRIGGERS. RESTRICT fails only when a referenced moment changes, following the SQL standard and DB2 for z/OS.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the series because it depended on FOR PORTION OF, which was reverted from v19. He plans to re-submit once FOR PORTION OF is done. No reviewer objected in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch series depended on FOR PORTION OF, which has been reverted
from v19. So I will mark it as Withdrawn for now.

precedents_retrieved.summary:
Indeterminate behavior for the GROUP BY clause
Section: Features We Do Not Want
Linked: Re: SQL compatibility reminder: MySQL vs PostgreSQL
precedents_retrieved.objection: At least one other database product allows specification of a subset of the result columns which GROUP BY would need to be able to provide predictable results; the server is free to return any value from the group. precedents_retrieved.title: remove_useless_groupby_columns is too enthusiastic
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change remove_useless_groupby_columns so that it no longer removes GROUP BY items that are functionally dependent on a primary key when those items also appear in ORDER BY. This keeps the link between the GROUP BY and ORDER BY lists, so the planner can use a sorted index path with GroupAggregate and avoid an explicit sort.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers pointed out that keeping the redundant columns can make plans worse. Without a matching index, the extra sort columns cost more (Richard Guo measured a slowdown). Hash Aggregate would always pay for hashing and comparing the extra columns. David Rowley proposed a different design: mark redundant GROUP BY columns instead of removing them, and consider both the full and the minimal key sets. No revised patch followed, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback after the thread had been idle for some weeks following that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So the
patch makes that case worse in favour of possibly making Group
Aggregate cases better.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pageinspect - add functions on GIN and GiST indexes from gevel
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alexander Korotkov, Tomas Vondra, Ashutosh Sharma, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the gevel module's functions for GiST, SP-GiST and GIN indexes into pageinspect, with tests and docs. The functions show whole-index statistics, print the tree and its stored objects, and estimate GIN value counts and query matches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the functions read the whole index, while pageinspect inspects single pages, so the code belongs in a new extension or should be rewritten as page-level functions. Peter Eisentraut also found that the patch no longer compiled and that the stats functions returned one formatted text value where they should return a row with columns. The author planned a new contrib module but posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after three weeks of waiting on the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The proposed patch uses a very different approach, reading the whole index,
not individual pages. Why should it be part of pageinspect?

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposed the same idea. P11 shows a grouping feature reverted because it mixed equality semantics, which supports this fix rather than arguing against it, and P6 and P24 do not apply. Two points could not be checked here: the size of the backpatch behaviour change (message #2), and whether release notes will warn about queries that start to fail.
Both objections concern how the fix is backpatched. Neither is against fixing the wrong-results bug.
The patch adds no WAL, on-disk format or wire protocol change, and no new catalog column. The objection covers only catalog state that already exists in 18.x clusters.

The patch has no privilege or exposure aspect. It makes the planner stricter about functional dependency, adds no object, privilege or setting, and gives no user access to data, sessions or resources they lacked before. Backpatch compatibility and pg_dump restore of existing views are other angles.

From the maintenance angle, the patch narrows a feature to btree indexes in one file, and adds no GUC, API or hot-path cost. Yilin Zhang raised the queries that now fail (message #2), and Andres Freund answered that the simpler fix is intended (message #4). The backpatch break remains unsized, and the patch does not yet say whether release notes will warn about it.

This is a wrong-results bugfix that narrows check_functional_grouping to btree indexes, and no existing feature, extension or setting gives correct grouping results without it. Users who lose functional grouping can list the extra columns in GROUP BY, which is the usual alternative but does not replace the fix.

This is a wrong-results fix for a bug a committer reported, so demand is not in question. The cost to working temporal-key queries was raised in message #2, and the reporter accepted it in message #4.
